findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant type factories
findings.body:
`OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` gains a new abstract method `getShortcut()` with no default implementation. Third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations will no longer compile.

Already-compiled extensions are worse off. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls `getShortcut()` on every grant factory, so they will throw `AbstractMethodError` and server startup will fail.

Fix: provide a default implementation (for example, a derived or unknown shortcut) or handle a missing shortcut gracefully.

findings.title: Javadoc says shortcut is ~3 letters, but encoding requires exactly 2
findings.body:
The Javadoc says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters", and nothing validates its length.

The default encoder concatenates the shortcut into the token ID prefix. The decoder then rejects any prefix that is not exactly 6 characters and splits it at fixed 2-character offsets.

A custom grant following the documented guidance (3 letters) will produce token IDs that `getTokenContextFromTokenId` rejects with `IllegalArgumentException`. Fix: document that the shortcut must be exactly 2 characters and validate this in postInit.

findings.title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed from SPI class
findings.body:
The public `Context(Context)` copy constructor was deleted from `OAuth2GrantType.Context`. This class is part of the grant-type SPI, so any extension that uses it will break at compile or link time.

If the copy constructor is kept, it must also copy the new `grantType` field.

findings.title: Null check for rawTokenId actually checks grantType again
findings.body:
`Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks `grantType` a second time. `rawTokenId` is never validated.

A null raw ID is therefore accepted silently. It later produces token IDs like `onrtac:null` instead of failing fast. The call should be `requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong offset and inverted condition, so it never checks grant type
findings.body:
The grant shortcut sits at indices 4-6 of the prefix, but the matcher uses `substring(3, 5)`, which yields e.g. "ta" for "onrtac". It also returns false when that substring *equals* the expected shortcut, which is the inverse of the intended check.

The wrong substring never equals a real shortcut, so the matcher accepts any `xxx:UUID` value. None of the integration tests actually verify that the expected grant type is encoded. The check should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes because of an NPE, not the intended validation
findings.body:
The test factory never calls `postInit`, so `sessionFactory` is null. For an unknown shortcut, `getGrantTypeByShortcut` calls `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)` and throws `NullPointerException`.

The test catches any `RuntimeException`, so it passes without ever exercising the "Unknown value for grant type" `IllegalArgumentException` path. It should catch `IllegalArgumentException` specifically and stub the session factory.

findings.title: Lazy grant-map refresh bypasses duplicate-shortcut validation
findings.body:
`postInit` validates that grant shortcuts are unique. The lazy refresh paths in `getShortcutByGrantType` and `getGrantTypeByShortcut` do not: they blindly `put` into both maps.

A hot-deployed grant with a shortcut that collides with an existing one silently overwrites `grantsByShortcuts`. Tokens issued under the original grant would then decode to the wrong grant type.
